FX-LIGHTX-001.says: FX-BOLT-001's settings with the five new ones written at their starting values (type direction, turbulence 0, decay 0, conductivity 0, obstacle 0): exactly FX-BOLT-001.

FX-LIGHTX-002.says: A straight line across row 4 from right to left, from (110, 45) to (-10, 45) per cent, width 1, no glow, with Alpha Obstacle 50 over the night sky's left half: it stops where it meets the sky. Columns 8 to 15 of row 4 lit, columns 0 to 6 untouched.

FX-LIGHTX-003.says: FX-LIGHTX-002 with Alpha Obstacle 0: the whole row lit, as before.

FX-LIGHTX-004.says: A jagged bolt from the middle of the top edge to the middle of the bottom, width 1, no glow, over a drawing whose rows 7 to 9 are ground, with Alpha Obstacle 50: it ends where it reaches the ground, and row 9 is untouched. Tutorial 2's bolt ending on the ground.

FX-LIGHTX-005.says: FX-LIGHTX-004 with Alpha Obstacle 0: the bolt runs on through the ground to the bottom edge.

FX-LIGHTX-006.says: FX-LIGHTX-004 with branches 100: the forks stop at the ground too.

FX-LIGHTX-007.says: FX-LIGHTX-004 over ground that half covers, Alpha Obstacle 40: half covering is not enough to block at 40, so the bolt runs to the bottom, as FX-LIGHTX-005 does on that drawing.

FX-LIGHTX-008.says: FX-LIGHTX-007 at Alpha Obstacle 60: now half covering blocks, and the bolt ends at the ground.

FX-LIGHTX-009.says: FX-BOLT-010's bolt (branches 100) as Strike: the main bolt the same, its forks turned from the way to the end point instead.

FX-LIGHTX-010.says: FX-BOLT-010's bolt as Breaking: the main bolt and the forks' paths the same, each fork starting as bright and as wide as the bolt where it leaves it.

FX-LIGHTX-011.says: FX-BOLT-009's bolt as Bouncy: three bolts between the two points, there, back and there again, each its own shape.

FX-LIGHTX-012.says: Omni from the middle, (50, 50), with the end point 3 pixels above it: six bolts 3 pixels long, 60 degrees apart, the first straight up.

FX-LIGHTX-013.says: Anywhere from the middle, the end point 3 pixels above it, hold 1: one bolt to somewhere within 3 pixels, a new place each frame.

FX-LIGHTX-014.says: Vertical from (25, 0), the end point at (90, 30): a bolt from column 4 of the top edge straight down to the bottom edge; the end point is not used.

FX-LIGHTX-015.says: FX-LIGHTX-014 with the end point at (10, 80): the same.

FX-LIGHTX-016.says: Two-Way Striking from the top edge's middle to the bottom's: two bolts, one down from the top and one up from the bottom, meeting in the middle.

FX-LIGHTX-017.says: FX-BOLT-001 with turbulence 100: a rougher bolt with more forks.

FX-LIGHTX-018.says: FX-BOLT-006's line (rows 4 and 5, width 2, left to right) with decay 100: thick at the left, thinning to nothing at the right.

FX-LIGHTX-019.says: FX-BOLT-009's bolt held for 100 frames, its conductivity keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 2 at frame 4: frame 0 is FX-BOLT-009's frame 0; the bolt changes shape smoothly through frames 1 to 4 without being redrawn.

FX-LIGHTX-020.says: A lightning type "sideways". The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-LIGHTX-021.says: Turbulence 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-LIGHTX-022.says: Decay -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-LIGHTX-023.says: Conductivity 10001, above 10000. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-LIGHTX-024.says: Alpha Obstacle 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
